sentences.text: Vijay vs Aditya Singh on 4 September, 2025

1   IN THE HIGH COURT OF MADHYA PRADESH  AT INDORE  BEFORE  HON'BLE SHRI JUSTICE PAVAN KUMAR DWIVEDI  ON THE 4 th OF SEPTEMBER, 2025  MISC. APPEAL No. 43 of 2023  VIJAY  Versus  ADITYA SINGH AND OTHERS  Appearance:

entities.text: HIGH COURT OF MADHYA PRADESH  AT INDORE
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Shri Sanjay Patwa, learned counsel for the appellan  Ms. Dilkush Kumawat, Advocate on behalf of Ms. Pree  learned counsel for the respondent No.3.

ORDER The appellant has filed this appeal under Section 173 of the Motor Vehicles Act being aggrieved by the award dated 25.03.2022 passed in claim case No.39/2021 challenging the quantum of compensation.
2. The liability of the insurance company due to injuries in the accident by the insured vehicle is not under dispute.

3. The short facts of the case are that on 10.02.2019 at around 06 O' clock in the evening the appellant was going by motorcycle from Jobat to village Badaguda, when he reached near village Rampura, the respondent No.1 came driving bus No.MP45-P-1701 in a rash and negligent manner and collided with the appellant head-on because of which the appellant sustain grievous injuries.

He was rushed to government hospital, Jobat from where he was referred to Jenab Nursing Home,
Dahod where he remained hospitalized 2 MA-43-2023 from 11.02.2019 to 28.02.2019.
He was operated upon his right leg and implant of rod was inserted.
He also suffered fracture in right hand.
4. The appellant filed claim petition under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act claiming compensation for the injuries sustained by him.
The claims tribunal after assessing the evidence awarded total sum of Rs.2,47,376/- to the appellant.

5. Learned counsel for the appellant submits that the claims tribunal also believed the permanent disability certificate Ex.P-18 inasmuch as permanent disability into his right hand to the extent of 27%, however, the permanent disability of 30% in his left eye has been discarded.
He submits that the claims tribunal could not have bifurcated the permanent disability certificate by believing one part of it and disbelieving other part of the same.
He submits that the permanent disability certificate has been issued by the district medical board, District-Alirajpur.
Thus, there was no occasion to the claims tribunal to disbelieve the extent of impairment in the left eye.

1 6.

Apart from this, the learned counsel for the appellant also submits that the appellant claimed the income of Rs.7500/- per month by doing the work of labourer but the claims tribunal has incorrectly disbelieved the same and on notional basis his income has been taken as Rs.4800/- per month.

Although even if the income of the appellant is considered on notional basis still in terms of the guidelines issued by the State Legal Services Authority, the minimum wages for an unskilled labourer at the relevant time was Rs.7325/-.
Apart from this, he also pointed out that meager amount has been awarded for special diet, conveyance and attendant charges, thus, prays for 3 MA-43-2023 enhancement of compensation.

7. Per contra, learned counsel for the insurance company submits that the claims tribunal has correctly discarded permanent impairment in the left eye of the appellant looking to the statement of Dr. K.C. Gupta PW-2, who has accepted in his cross examination that there was no injury in left eye of the appellant.
He thus submits that the findings of the claims tribunal are correct.

8. As regards the income, learned counsel for the respondent submits that there was no proof at all for establishing the income of appellant as Rs.7500/- per month, hence, the claims tribunal has correctly assessed the income of the appellant on notional basis, hence, he prays for dismissal of the appeal.

9. Heard the learned counsel for the parties and perused the record.
10.
From perusal of the record of the claims tribunal, it is reflected that the appellant suffered grievous injuries on various parts of his body.
He has suffered head injuries and compound comminuted fracture of humerus bone and fracture in his right hand and right foot.
His right hand and right leg were operated upon and implant of rod was put into it.
He remained hospitalized for a period from 11.02.2019 to 28.02.2019.
Apart from this period, he remained under treatment for a long period.
At the time of accident, the appellant is stated to be working as a labourer.
11. The claims tribunal considered the issue of permanent disability from para 15 to 20 of the impugned award.

After referring to Ex.P-18 the permanent disability certificate as well as statement of Dr. K.C. Gupta, PW- 4 MA-43-2023 2, the claims tribunal concluded that the permanent disability into the right upper limb of the appellant as 27% is found proved.

However, with respect to permanent disability into left eye to the extent of 30% was not believed and as such the over all permanent disability with respect to loss of earning capacity has been taken at 9%.
12. In the considered view of this Court, the conclusion of the claims tribunal in taking the permanent disability at 9% is not correct.
Only for the reason that there was no direct injuries into the left eye of the appellant, the medical certificate of the medical district board is discarded.
It was undisputed that the appellant suffered head injuries in the accident.
No doubt it is opined that he suffered 30% visual impairment due to said injuries.
If the claims tribunal was of the view that the certificate of permanent disability with respect to left eye is not correct then it should have got it examined again by an expert.

Vijay vs Aditya Singh on 4 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/74276351/
2 13.
Considering the over all circumstances of the present case, over all permanent disability with respect to loss of earning capacity is taken at 15%.

As regards the income of the appellant, as the claims tribunal itself has treated the appellant as unskilled labourer, thus, in terms of guidelines issued by State Legal Services Authority, the minimum wages for unskilled labour on the date of the accident i.e. on 10.02.2019 at Rs.7325/- is taken as income of the appellant.
In view of the above changed parameters, the compensation for loss of earning capacity would now come to Rs.2,76,840/-.

14. As regards the compensation for special diet, conveyance and attendant charges, the same is modified to Rs.30,000/- and for loss of earning 5 MA-43-2023 during the period of treatment Rs.21,975/- is awarded by taking the period of treatment of 3 months.
Now, the total compensation comes to Rs.4,74,931/-.

After deducting the amount already awarded by the claims tribunal at Rs.2,47,376/-, the appellant is now entitled for payment of Rs.2,77,555/- over and above the amount already awarded by the claims tribunal.
This enhanced amount shall carry interest @6% per annum from the date of application before the claims tribunal.
15. As the appeal has been valued at Rs.2 Lacs, the appellant has to pay deficit court fees within a period of four weeks from today.
If the court fees is not paid within this period then interest shall not apply on the enhanced amount of compensation beyond the period of 4 weeks.
16. With the aforesaid, the present appeal stands disposed of.

(PAVAN KUMAR DWIVEDI) JUDGE N.R.
